match_note: Referees quote v1 text verbatim (the 'AFMTJ' acronym, 'magnetic domain size range of ~100-170 nm', 'vanished at temperatures above 360 K', the Onsager reciprocity sentence on page 4, NV films on MgO (100)), and refer to Fig. 1c STEM, Fig. 2a-d and Extended Data Figs 1-2 as in v1. Referee #2 only co-reviewed with another referee and wrote no separate report. The file contains the author rebuttals to rounds 1 and 3 but not to round 2.

concerns.quote: The authors should provide evidence that their layers are free of ferromagnetic clusters, such as X-ray diffraction, magnetization measurements, or simple transport measurements
concerns.summary: Room-temperature-deposited, unannealed Mn3Pt may not be in the noncollinear antiferromagnetic phase and may contain ferromagnetic secondary phases; structural and magnetic evidence is needed.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the AFMs have adjacent Pt layers, which could be a source of spin-orbit torque (SOT)... without a proper control experiment, one cannot rule out this origin of the switching.
concerns.summary: Switching could be driven by spin-orbit torque from the adjacent Pt layers rather than octupole-driven spin-transfer torque, and no control experiment excludes this.

concerns.quote: other mechanisms related to “high” current density could be involved. Previous literature examples have shown that thin tunnel barriers can exhibit current-driven resistance changes regardless of magnetic properties
concerns.summary: Because TMR is inferred only from current-switching curves, non-magnetic current-driven resistance changes in the thin barrier could mimic the signal.

concerns.quote: I miss a standard TMR with applied magnetic field, as in Refs. 11 and 12. This will help compare the magnitudes of the direct (TMR) and reciprocal (OTT) effect.
concerns.summary: A conventional field-swept TMR measurement is missing and is needed to correlate with the current-switching TMR.

concerns.quote: It is difficult to accept the findings from one sample to support the results of a presumably relatively different sample.
concerns.summary: The NV-magnetometry domain sizes come from epitaxial, high-temperature films on MgO, unlike the junction stack, so extrapolating them to the devices is questionable.

concerns.quote: there is also an extremely large dispersion among the measured devices, with very few occurrences of large values. I wonder about the reliability of the TMR, the reason for the wide spread
concerns.summary: The TMR distribution across devices is very broad with few large values, and its origin and the reliability of the headline TMR need explaining.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the observation of this octupole-driven spin-transfer torque (OTT) is an expected follow-up after the groundbreaking reports in refs. 11-13, which from my point of view limits the impact
concerns.summary: Given prior TMR reports in antiferromagnetic tunnel junctions and Onsager reciprocity, the torque is an expected follow-up of limited impact.

concerns.quote: The nice plateau after switching is shown only once (Fig. 2b); but in the supplementary material, all devices below 100 nm exhibit gradual switching.
concerns.summary: The role of domain size versus pillar size, and whether domain nucleation or wall motion causes gradual multilevel switching, needs fuller discussion.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: It seems that each figure is made from different devices with varying properties. Can the authors provide clarification? Do the devices break down easily?
concerns.summary: Each figure uses a different device, raising questions about endurance and device selection.

concerns.quote: How many times were the devices cycled to extract switching current, how large are the variations cycle to cycle?
concerns.summary: The number of switching cycles and the cycle-to-cycle variation of switching current are not reported.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Is this behavior irreversible when cooling down, and was the vanishing of properties above 360 K observed in all devices tested?
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the loss of switching and TMR above 360 K is reversible on cooling and seen in all devices.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the authors should specify in the methods how the PtMn3 is made (co-deposition or stoichiometric target) and provide the real stoichiometry of the layers
concerns.summary: The deposition method and measured stoichiometry of PtMn3 are not given.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: Can such high TMR values be expected given that the MgO is not crystallized?
concerns.summary: Very large TMR is surprising for an amorphous MgO barrier and needs justification.

concerns.quote: The MgO thickness is indicated to be 2 nm, but the resistance-area (RA) product is in the range of 1-10 Ω·cm². To my understanding, at 2 nm MgO, the RA should be larger.
concerns.summary: The reported RA product seems too low for a 2 nm MgO barrier.

concerns.quote: In Fig. 2a, the switching current densities seem slightly asymmetric for the two polarities. Could the authors comment on this issue in the main text?
concerns.summary: The asymmetry of switching currents between the two polarities is not discussed.

concerns.quote: It is unclear whether the STEM image in Fig. 1c is from an actual AFMTJ pillar or from the stack before the etching.
concerns.summary: The origin of the STEM cross-section in Fig. 1c (patterned pillar or unpatterned stack) is unstated.

concerns.quote: the term/abbreviation AATJ shall be utilized throughout the entire manuscript including the extended data, in place of AFMTJ.
concerns.summary: Use the more widely adopted acronym AATJ instead of AFMTJ.

concerns.quote: Could they speculate on which kind of band structure features or material systems might exhibit stronger OTT?
concerns.summary: The outlook should suggest band-structure features or materials that could give stronger torque.

concerns.quote: a paragraph of discussion in the outlook speculating on the potential switching speed limits of OTT
concerns.summary: The outlook should discuss the potential switching-speed limits of the torque.

later_concerns.quote: I find it puzzling that there is no magnetic field characterization of TMR and spin transport by AHE... I want to see it.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: still requests field-swept TMR and anomalous Hall transport to characterise the antiferromagnet and which electrode reverses.

later_concerns.quote: can the authors explain why some R-I loops have opposite chirality, e.g., as seen in Extended Data Fig. 1?
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: some current-switching loops have opposite chirality, unexplained.

later_concerns.quote: To me, they appear to be outlier occurrences—I would expect more statistics to support this.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: the largest TMR values look like outliers and the termination explanation needs more statistics; low RA conflicts with the large-TMR explanation.

later_concerns.quote: one cannot assume that an asymmetry uniquely signals OTT in this system... the arguments used to exclude an SOT origin are weak.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: switching-current asymmetry does not exclude SOT; asks for in-plane current through Pt, a W or low-spin-Hall seed, or polarizer reversal by field cooling.

later_concerns.quote: I would not expect similar magnetic domain sizes in not compensated (001) and fully compensated (111) samples
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: comparing domain sizes of uncompensated (001) and compensated (111) films remains questionable.

later_concerns.quote: Previous reports on Mn₃Pt do observe a finite net moment... the authors' hypothesis... may not be valid.
later_concerns.summary: Round 2: zero net moment in polycrystalline films conflicts with literature and with the epitaxial-strain hypothesis.

later_concerns.quote: performing R-V loops at large fields, even at ±1T, would provide a striking demonstration of the device immunity to external fields.
later_concerns.summary: Round 3: asks for switching loops under large fields to show field immunity; still doubts termination explanation given polycrystalline averaging.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: The most decisive experiment I suggested, reversing the magnetic state of the top “polarizer” layer... has not been performed
later_concerns.summary: Round 3: the polarizer-reversal field-cooling test is still missing, and transient heating toward the Néel temperature is not excluded.
later_concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

later_concerns.quote: the use of only ±0.2 T for the field cooling process, that might not be large enough to control the octupole direction
later_concerns.summary: Round 4: field-cooling field may be too small; recommends publication anyway.
